ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: FINTRAC-compliant KYC: mandatory match of all directors, officers, UBOs and signatories against PEP lists, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions, OFAC SDN (where USD or US-correspondent banking is used), and UN Security Council consolidated lists. Enhanced due diligence for PEPs, high-risk country transactions and irregular payment routes; re-screening at least every 90 days and at each material ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Enterprise Register / nom-reservation portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate name must be expressed in French unless a statutory exception is obtained; non-French words require supporting documentation and a French descriptor; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; ‘Inc.’, ‘Corp.’ or ‘Ltée’ may serve as the legal element; each name must include a distinctive element and be distinct from existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 120 days; if not used within the window, the applicant must file a fresh reservation. If the Registraire rejects the name, the written refusal states the statutory ground; the applicant may either submit a corrected name or request administrative reconsideration. An administrative appeal should be filed within 30 days of the refusal; if refused, judicial review may be brought before the Court of Québec (Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01) within 30 days of the review decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. The office must be a real, staffed municipal address in Quebec where service of process and corporate records can be received. For the frozen beef/seafood importer, a cold-chain operations address with an administrative suite, or a physical executive office together with a licensed warehouse, is recommended; a mail-forwarding virtual box alone is insufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10% risk of an unannounced corporate-registered-office inspection; approximately 60–70% risk of Canadian Food Inspection Agency/MAPAQ cold-chain inspection around the first customs release; combined unannounced audit risk about 35% in the first fiscal year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, arts. 12-26 (incorporation), 117 (directors), 213 (by-laws), 214 (officers); Regulation respecting Business Corporations, CQLR c S-31.1, r. 1
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Direction des sociétés par actions
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The consideration for issued shares must be fixed by the board and fully paid before share certificates are issued, unless shares are issued for future services, in which case issuance occurs only after complete performance. No escrow account requirement is imposed under the corporate registering statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscriptions for shares set out in the Articles of Incorporation are accepted, and the Secretary is directed to issue share certificates to the subscribers. 2. The registered office of the Corporation is established at [Street Address, City, Province of Quebec, Postal Code], as stated in the Articles, and is adopted as the Corporation’s head office. 3. The Corporation’s by-laws governing the administration and management of the Corporation are adopted and ratified. 4. [Name of Director] is appointed director of the Corporation, and [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively, to act until the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Online Enterprise Name Search and CLIC platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a compulsory name search using the REQ's name search service. Submit a request for name reservation (Attestation de réservation de nom) indicating the corporate name comprised of distinctive, descriptive and legal elements. The reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (distinctive element, descriptive element, legal element 'Inc.' or 'Corp.')
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new name reservation request with a revised distinctive element or submit an administrative review request to REQ within 30 days, attaching the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and authentication of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators / notary in the province of Quebec (optional for the statutory instrument; notarization is often required by banks or commercial counterparties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed REQ form under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. When the incorporator is a natural person, signature is sufficient; when it is a legal entity, signature must be made by two authorized officers or by an attorney holding a written resolution. Optional notarization is recommended to expedite banking and commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director form for each named director
Certificate of legal existence of corporate incorporator (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft contains inconsistencies, amend and re-execute before filing; if a notary has issued a certificate, request a notarial corrective deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of articles and issuance of certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – CLIC secure electronic filing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Articles of Incorporation and the prescribed filing fee to REQ through the CLIC portal. Upon validation, REQ automatically issues the certificate of incorporation and assigns the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). The corporation comes into existence on the date stated on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director forms
Corporate postal address and registered office elements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ raises a query (demande de renseignements), respond within 30 days via CLIC; failure to respond causes the file to be treated as abandoned, requiring a new submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of initial declaration and receipt of Quebec enterprise number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Declaration processing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation) is filed with the articles and contains the registered office, directors and the principal Quebec address. In an electronic filing, this declaration is processed simultaneously with the articles, and upon completion the corporation obtains its NEQ and registration record.
required_dossiers: Registered office and mailing address in Quebec
Nature of the principal business activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial declaration is rejected, a corrected declaration must be filed online; a modification to an already registered declaration can be made through the REQ portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and provincial tax accounts enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Québec – enterprise account via 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a CRA Business Number and request GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts if applicable. Register with Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), employer contributions and other provincial accounts. Provide the NEQ and link the accounts through the CRA-Revenu Québec electronic services.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account details for direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec issues a query, correct the registration online or call the business telephone line; invalid registrations may be amended without restarting the incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational meeting, by-law adoption and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the corporation / Board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or execute a written resolution in lieu. Adopt the general by-law, approve share issuance and share certificates, select the corporate seal (optional), appoint officers, approve bank signing authorities and adopt the minute book. Update REQ records if officers are registered.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice / consent to hold first meeting
Share subscription forms and share certificates
Resolution electing directors and appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum defect is discovered, cure it by executing a unanimous written resolution of all directors ratified at the next meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Safe Food for Canadians Act import licence and Quebec food import permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) – Regulatory Trading Partner Portal ('My CFIA'); Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) – Bureau de l'inspection des aliments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the import of frozen beef and pelagic fish, obtain a licence under the Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) applicable to food importers. Submit the licence application through My CFIA, indicating commodity classes 'meat' and 'fish' and providing a preventive control plan summary. Concurrently file a MAPAQ permit application under the Food Products Act (CQLR c P-29) for the importation of foodstuffs.
required_dossiers: Commodity classification (HS codes for frozen beef and seafood)
Sanitary documentation from country of origin
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CFIA or MAPAQ issues a notice of deficiency, submit corrected information within 30 days; repeated refusal triggers the right of administrative review before the respective administrative bodies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) and Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence – Importation of Food (CFIA) and Food Import Permit (MAPAQ, CQLR c P-29)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a wholesale import and refrigerated storage operation and does not alter land or install fixed industrial equipment subject to section 31.1 of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC thresholds apply to pure import operations; any refrigeration installation must comply with CEPA, 1999 Schedule 3 halocarbon regulations and Quebec's Regulation respecting halocarbons, ensuring leak detection and refrigerant recovery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certification (permis d'affaires including fire values), structural load certificates for cold storage racking, and CNESST workplace health and safety clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada – Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) via Mon dossier d'entreprise; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs import/export accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online (Form RC1 or online application). Step 2: Register for the GST/HST (RT) account and the Import/Export (RM) account. Step 3: Register for QST with Revenu Québec via Form LM-101-V or online once a commercial activity is carried on in Québec. Step 4: If applicable, appoint a licensed customs broker and establish a CBSA importer/exporter bond and security account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' election is available for Canadian corporations. Elective mechanisms include: (i) GST/HST Quick Method election for qualifying SMEs (ETA s. 227 reference); (ii) QST simplified accounting method election; (iii) election under ETA s. 273 and analogous QST provisions for zero-rated intercompany supplies between closely related corporations; (iv) treaty-based classification of fiscally transparent foreign entities (e.g., US LLCs) under Canada-US Tax Convention Art. IV(7) as administered by the CRA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) – dual VAT-type consumption taxes administered federally by the CRA and provincially by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST small-supplier threshold, Excise Tax Act s. 148; QST small-supplier threshold, Québec Taxation Act s. 402). Importers of taxable goods into Canada must pay GST/QST at the border regardless of registration status; registration is mandatory above the CAD 30,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada. Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST and QST returns applies to registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million (GST/HST NETFILE; Revenu Québec e-services). Import/export declarations are transmitted electronically to the CBSA through the CARM (CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management) platform, with border GST/QST assessed via integrated broker EDI messaging (ACI/ACKNACK).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST/QST applies to tangible personal property (including frozen beef and seafood) exported by the supplier or under the supplier's direction, per ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 5 and the corresponding QST provisions. Services in respect of the exported goods or performed for non-residents may be zero-rated where they do not relate to Canadian real property (ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7). The exporter must retain contemporaneous evidence of physical export, transfer of ownership, and payment to substantiate the claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or CARM e-Export Report)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent FX settlement proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rating claims within four years, with no limitation period in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or gross negligence. Clawback of claimed refunds is accompanied by statutory interest. Penalties include: 25% of the net tax misstatement under Excise Tax Act s. 280(1); 50% gross-negligence penalty under Income Tax Act s. 163(2); criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239 with fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment; and analogous QST penalties under the Québec Taxation Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls or mandatory conversion of commercial foreign-currency receipts. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated deposit-taking institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada administers anti-money-laundering and anti-terrorist-financing reporting requirements; the Canada Revenue Agency administers tax reporting and transfer-pricing requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and capital transactions. Canada generally permits unrestricted inbound and outbound investment, dividend payments, interest payments, loan repayments, and trade settlements, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax withholding, corporate-law solvency requirements, contractual banking restrictions, and accurate underlying-transaction documentation. There is no routine approval requirement for a Canadian corporation to purchase or remit foreign currency. A Quebec corporation may receive foreign capital through its Canadian bank account, maintain foreign-currency accounts, and remit lawful profits to non-resident shareholders. Dividends must be declared in accordance with applicable corporate law, including solvency requirements, and non-resident withholding tax commonly applies at the Canadian domestic rate of 25 percent unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty. Interest, royalties, management fees, and other cross-border payments may also attract withholding tax and transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, deductibility, and treaty-entitlement review. The Importer of Record must maintain customs, tax, sanctions, origin, valuation, and food-import records for frozen beef and seafood. Canadian banks may require enhanced evidence for high-value related-party funding, unusual jurisdictions, cash-intensive activity, rapid fund movements, or transactions involving sanctioned parties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No Canadian statutory rule requires exporters to repatriate or surrender export proceeds to a Canadian bank, convert a prescribed percentage of export receipts, or convert receipts within a prescribed statutory period. Export proceeds may generally remain in Canadian or foreign-currency accounts, subject to tax, accounting, sanctions, customs, contractual, and anti-money-laundering obligations. For this business model, which is primarily an importer and wholesale distributor, the principal FX-control issue is payment for imports rather than surrender of export proceeds. Banks may nevertheless impose contractual reporting, documentary, or transaction-monitoring requirements and may request invoices, bills of lading, customs entries, purchase orders, and beneficial-owner information.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment functionality and Low to Medium as a substitute for a principal Canadian operating bank. A foreign electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide collection, foreign-exchange, and cross-border payout services only within the scope of its home-jurisdiction licence and the Canadian regulatory perimeter. An offshore provider does not automatically have authority to conduct deposit-taking, retail payment services, money services, or payment activities in Canada. The corporation should verify whether the provider is registered with FINTRAC where required, registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act regime if applicable and in force for its activities, permitted to hold client funds, and capable of satisfying Canadian sanctions, source-of-funds, recordkeeping, privacy, and payment-transparency requirements. Customer funds may not have the same deposit-insurance or creditor-protection status as deposits at a Canadian deposit-taking institution. Use of an offshore EMI should be limited to documented treasury corridors, with a Canadian bank retained for payroll, taxes, customs, supplier settlement, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance by directors is not generally mandated by Canadian law for opening a corporate bank account. Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding, electronic signatures, video identification, and notarized or certified corporate documents, subject to their internal risk policies. A director, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, or controlling person may nevertheless be required to attend a video or in-person interview, provide government-issued identification, complete liveness checks, or attend a branch where the ownership chain, foreign control, business model, expected transaction volume, high-risk geography, or documentation cannot be verified remotely. Quebec corporations may additionally need to provide French-language or bilingual corporate and operating documents where requested by the institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent corporate records, including missing articles, certificate of incorporation, corporate registry profile, register of directors, share ownership records, or signing authority evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified or bank-acceptable copies of articles and certificate of incorporation, current Quebec or federal corporate registry extract, corporate profile report, bylaws, board resolutions authorizing accounts and signatories, shareholder register, organizational chart, and current director and officer list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, bearer-style ownership, layered foreign holding companies, or inability to identify individuals who own or control the corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership chart tracing every legal entity to natural persons, certified identity and address documents for each beneficial owner and controlling person, shareholder agreements, trust deeds where relevant, control analysis, beneficial-ownership declaration, and written explanation of any nominee or minority-protection arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder, director, parent, lender, or supplier located in a sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or opaque jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full jurisdiction map, sanctions-screening results, passports and proof of address, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, tax-residency information, banking references, contractual counterparties, compliance certifications, and documented prohibition of sanctioned counterparties and prohibited trade routes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or unusual inbound capital described only as 'investment' or 'loan' without a clear legal instrument and commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement, shareholder-loan agreement or intercompany financing agreement, board approvals, capitalization table, beneficial-owner funding trail, lender financial statements, source-of-funds records, transfer-pricing support where applicable, and wire instructions matching the legal instrument.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frozen beef and seafood trade involving complex chains, third-party payments, cash transactions, unusual transit routes, or counterparties whose names do not match invoices and shipping documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier and customer master files, purchase and sales contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, customs declarations, import permits and licences, CFIA-related documentation, cold-chain records, proof of delivery, payment-flow diagram, and written explanation for any third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained expected account activity, including large foreign-currency turnover, rapid pass-through of funds, large cash deposits, or material divergence between the stated business plan and actual transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast, monthly currency and country matrix, expected transaction volumes and ticket sizes, working-capital model, supplier and customer concentration report, treasury policy, bank-statement history, tax filings where available, and documented escalation procedures for unusual transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions, export-control, customs, food-safety, or trade-based money-laundering exposure in beef and seafood imports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty sanctions screening, product classification, country-of-origin and tariff records, import eligibility evidence, CFIA and CBSA compliance file, valuation methodology, quantity and price benchmarking, restricted-party screening, end-use and end-user statements, and independent compliance review for higher-risk shipments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, undisclosed cash collection, commingling of shareholder funds with operating receipts, or unexplained related-party transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dedicated corporate banking policy, accounting ledger, intercompany-reconciliation schedule, board-approved related-party transaction policy, shareholder funding records, prohibition on personal-account use, bank statements, and corrective-action evidence for any historical commingling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, corruption, or litigation concerns involving directors, owners, agents, or major counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-residency self-certifications, PEP declarations, litigation and insolvency searches, adverse-media analysis, professional references, compliance questionnaires, anti-bribery policy, beneficial-owner interviews, and written remediation or independent legal opinions where an alert is not substantiated.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian commercial bank to the corporation's designated Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency account. The remitter name should match the shareholder or disclosed funding entity, and the payment reference should identify the legal instrument, such as share subscription, paid-in capital, or shareholder loan. Before remittance, provide the bank with the executed financing documents, board approvals, capitalization or loan schedule, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner information, and expected amount and currency. Use the bank's accurate payment-purpose classification; Canada does not impose a universal statutory FX purpose-code system for ordinary corporate wires, but banks require truthful internal purpose descriptions and may require a SWIFT purpose narrative, invoice reference, or loan and equity classification. Do not characterize a loan as equity or trade payment as an investment. Reconcile receipt to the general ledger, issue share certificates or record the loan as legally appropriate, retain SWIFT confirmation and bank statements, and review withholding-tax, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, interest-deductibility, and shareholder-benefit implications before any onward payment. Large or unusual transfers may be reported by the financial institution to FINTRAC under applicable reporting rules without that report indicating unlawful conduct.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary supplier payments, use a Canadian bank foreign-currency account and a SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly represented by an MT103 message or its ISO 20022 successor, with the exact beneficiary legal name, account or IBAN where applicable, BIC, bank address, invoice number, purchase-order number, goods description, and shipment reference. For new, high-value, or higher-risk suppliers, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a Canadian bank, with compliant presentation of commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, inspection or health documents, and insurance documents where required. A revolving letter of credit may support recurring frozen-food purchases if shipment periods, drawing limits, tolerances, expiry, sanctions wording, and discrepancy procedures are clearly defined. Use correspondent banks and payment corridors approved by the bank; screen all parties and vessels where relevant; avoid third-party payments unless documented and pre-approved; and reconcile customs values, invoices, landed costs, GST or HST, duties, freight, and inventory records. Supplier prepayments should be supported by a contract, invoice, advance-payment terms, counterparty due diligence, and evidence of subsequent shipment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, used to hedge documented forecast or contracted USD, EUR, or other currency payables and receivables. Maintain hedge documentation, tenor limits, counterparty limits, settlement instructions, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is restricted or where settlement is contractually designed in a freely convertible currency, subject to dealer eligibility, derivatives documentation, sanctions screening, and confirmation that the instrument is used for genuine commercial exposure rather than speculative trading.

Cross-currency swaps or currency swaps for documented shareholder loans, bank debt, inventory financing, or recurring long-term currency exposures, subject to credit support, collateral, netting, valuation, termination, and accounting requirements.

Foreign-exchange options, including purchased calls, puts, collars, and zero-cost structures, for protection against adverse currency movements while retaining participation in favorable movements. Avoid uncovered written options unless specifically approved under the treasury policy and understood as potentially leveraged obligations.

Interest-rate and cross-currency derivative transactions should be documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or equivalent dealer documentation, with confirmations identifying the hedged exposure, valuation method, collateral terms, early-termination rights, and applicable Canadian derivatives reporting or trade-repository requirements.

Do not use hedging instruments to conceal capital movements, bypass sanctions, create artificial trade invoices, or speculate beyond approved exposure limits. Reconcile every hedge to a forecast or executed commercial exposure and maintain board-approved treasury controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under Section 263 of the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of federal incorporation or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada after formal notice; a cessation order can also be issued and revival requires restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration / Mise à jour with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of registration in Quebec for an extra-provincial CBCA corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue at CAD 17.00 per day and may compound; prolonged non-compliance triggers cancellation of the registration, loss of legal personality in Quebec, and inability to enforce contracts or defend legal actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal period (tax year); for a calendar-year same as Canada, due June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months); repeated failure may trigger a late-filing penalty of 10% plus 2% per month; criminal prosecution is possible for wilful failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); additional penalty if tax not paid when due; interest is compounded daily.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory revenue or asset threshold in Quebec or under the CBCA for a privately held CBCA corporation. A non-distributing corporation that is not a reporting issuer may dispense with the annual audit by unanimous shareholder consent. Mandatory audit applies to reporting issuers, issuers distributing securities, and any corporation whose shareholders do not unanimously waive audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises or ASPE for private enterprises. Wholesale import companies incorporated under the CBCA may choose either IFRS or Quebec ASPE-equivalent, provided the choice is applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each annual return under the CBCA must confirm the existence and accuracy of the register of individuals with significant control; material share transfers or changes in significant control must be recorded in the register and reported to Corporations Canada and the REQ within the applicable statutory period (not exceeding 30 days for register updates). Annual Declaration to the REQ must include current beneficial owners and senior managers, with any change disclosed.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800–1,500 per year (registered office and annual agent service in Quebec)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 6,000–15,000 per fiscal year for a standalone mid-size private import corporation if audit is compulsory; 3,500–8,000 for a review engagement where audit is waived

stage_6.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of frozen beef and seafood resale revenue, fabrication of import invoices, off-book cash sales, or concealment of the Quebec permanent establishment to avoid Quebec tax.
stage_6.statutory_sanction: ITA s. 239(1): imprisonment up to 5 years (indictable) and/or fine of 50%–200% of the evaded tax; s. 163(2) gross-negligence civil penalty of 50% of the false overstatement; Revenu Québec penalties under the Tax Administration Act of up to 200% of the applicable tax (Quebec 'pénalité pour faute lourde'). Both CRA and Revenu Québec assess interest compounded daily.
stage_6.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal Code and ITA s. 242: directors, officers, and senior employees who participated in or acquiesced to evasion are personally prosecutable and subject to imprisonment; for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST, ITA s. 227.1 makes directors personally liable for the unremitted amounts plus interest and penalties without proof of intent.
